features.note: No regression at 30% travel: drive blade sweeps up with a bright streaked skin while top and bottom blades counter-tilt into dark undersides; adjacent blades never parallel. The new fine axial streaking on the drive blade follows the roll direction and reinforces the sheet-metal read.

Unchanged and strong: plated stub protrudes ~40-50 mm from the frame-face boss before the black U-clamp; the orange body hangs offset on the shaft, never flush. Anti-rotation strap runs down to a strap foot with plated hex hardware on the frame face.

Deferred printing now delivered: the actuator head carries a raised off-white bezel dial with a printed face — graduation ticks near the top of the sweep, a small printed caption below the hub, and a bold black tapered pointer with hub angled consistently with 30% travel on the shaft axis. It reads as a position gauge, completing pointer + printed 0-90 arc. Weakness: at this camera the wide pointer occludes much of the arc and the 0/90 end numerals are not resolvable; the gauge reads more by shape than by its printing. 1:1 rotation itself is unverifiable in a single frame; the pointer angle is at least consistent.

No regression: channel frame keeps real ~0.13 m depth, flange rings on both faces with discrete fastener heads and visible wall thickness. Surface pass adds a plausible ink stamp '600 x 400 GALV' on the bottom front rail — correct scale, matches the spec size callout — and mottling now covers the flat faces, not just the flange tops.

No regression: three crank blocks on the non-actuator side with the middle (drive) block tilted opposed to top/bottom, joined by a bright plated tie rod; unequal block spacing still betrays articulation consistent with 30% travel.

important_features.note: Unchanged from materials attempt 2: blade-edge EPDM strips read as discrete matte near-black bulbs along the blade long edges; lower jamb strips separate from the frame interior, the upper interior jamb seal still only faintly separates from shadow.

Improved as expected: the label is now a structured printed plate — BELIMO header with orange logo square, bold model line 'LM24A-SR', rule lines, ~6 rows of spec text, and a barcode with a numeric caption. At natural viewing scale it convincingly reads as a factory label; the body rows blur to pseudo-text only under extreme zoom.
Unchanged: dark cable exits below the actuator and droops in a curved catenary toward the floor; still dim against the dark floor and partially clipped by the CONTROL DE EQUIPO panel.

defects: Dial printing legibility: the graduation ticks cluster near the top of the sweep and are partially occluded by the wide pointer; the 0 and 90 end numerals are not resolvable at this camera angle, so the gauge identity leans on bezel/pointer shape more than on the printed arc.

The galvanized mottling reads as low-frequency angular/polygonal patches (triangular blobs) rather than crystalline spangle; convincing at scene scale, but at close range it could read as procedural noise. It does, however, now break uniformity on every flat frame face — the materials-pass frame-uniformity defect is resolved.

Carried from materials attempt 2: the drive blade still sits roughly one value family brighter than the frame sharing galv_steel, with a single soft dark reflection band instead of structured room content.

Carried from materials attempt 2 (deferred to lighting-camera): the upper interior of the opening remains the darkest zone; the top blade underside and upper jamb seal separate from shadow only marginally.
Single-view ambiguity (recorded per gate contract): all surface reads verified from one neutral view only; no grazing/look-dev capture accompanies this attempt, so scores are capped at 0.85.
corrections: Optional polish: shift or extend the dial's printed graduations so ticks and the 0/90 numerals sit clear of the pointer sweep at the spec camera (or thin the pointer toward the tip) so the arc printing, not just the pointer, carries the gauge read.
Optional polish: layer a finer, higher-frequency noise octave over the galv mottle so the patchiness reads as spangle rather than polygonal blobs under close inspection.
Carried to lighting-camera pass: add a faint secondary fill or slightly higher env intensity on the upper interior so the top blade underside and upper jamb seal read without inspection.
